forces.title: E-commerce and 3PL drive robust warehousing demand
forces.description: The industrial and warehousing sector experiences strong activity, primarily fueled by the expansion of e-commerce, the increasing reliance on third-party logistics (3PL) providers, and the growth of multimodal supply chains. These sectors' buoyant demand is a key underlying factor supporting the development and healthy occupancy levels of warehousing and logistics parks across India, ensuring sustained growth for the sub-industry.

forces.title: Digital technologies transform industrial real estate development and management
forces.description: Advanced digital capabilities like Building Information Modeling (BIM), digital twins, AI-supported analysis, and integrated construction management platforms are reshaping real estate development. These technologies enhance planning precision, improve cost and schedule discipline, and provide real-time performance oversight. For warehousing and logistics parks, this fundamentally impacts design, construction, and operational efficiency, leading to smarter and more predictable project outcomes.

forces.title: Real estate developers expanding into logistics as key asset class
forces.description: Major real estate developers are increasingly diversifying their portfolios to include emerging asset classes such as logistics. This strategic shift indicates a recognition of the strong demand and growth potential within the warehousing and logistics parks segment. Such diversification brings significant investment and development expertise into the sub-industry, potentially accelerating the supply of high-quality industrial real estate.

forces.title: Warehousing InvITs gaining traction as investment vehicles
forces.description: Warehousing Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) are an emerging and well-positioned segment within the broader InvIT market, supported by healthy occupancy levels and moderate leverage. These specialized investment vehicles offer a structured pathway for capital allocation into industrial real estate, reflecting growing institutional confidence and appetite for income-generating logistics assets, thereby expanding financing options for the sector.

forces.title: Institutional investment and public capex bolster real estate growth
forces.description: Rising institutional capital participation, including private equity funds and REITs, alongside a sixfold increase in government capital expenditure, is strengthening the infrastructure backbone and supporting sustained growth across the real estate sector. This influx of capital and strategic public spending provides a conducive environment for the expansion and modernization of warehousing and logistics parks, facilitating larger and more sophisticated developments.

forces.title: Green building movement drives sustainable and efficient real estate
forces.description: India's significant green building footprint, with over 7,000 IGBC-certified projects, highlights a growing trend towards sustainable construction. This movement offers substantial energy and water savings, leading to higher rental and market value premiums. Adopting green building practices in warehousing and logistics parks can enhance their appeal, attract environmentally conscious tenants, and ensure long-term operational efficiency and resilience.

forces.title: Increasing land and construction costs challenge warehousing yields
forces.description: Rising land prices and higher construction costs are posing significant near-term challenges for the warehousing and logistics park sector. These elevated input costs exert pressure on development viability and can compress rental yields, making it harder for developers and investors to achieve desired returns. This could potentially impact the pace of new supply and overall profitability for industrial real estate projects.

forces.title: Government digital reforms for land records enhance transparency and reduce acquisition risks
forces.description: Government initiatives, such as the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) and the target for 100% digitization of land records by December 2025, are fundamentally transforming land acquisition. These reforms reduce risks associated with title disputes and ownership uncertainties, streamlining the process for real estate projects, including the crucial land procurement for warehousing and logistics parks, thereby accelerating development.

forces.title: RBI policy allows bank lending to REITs, boosting liquidity
forces.description: The Reserve Bank of India's February 2026 decision to permit banks to lend to REITs under regulatory safeguards enhances liquidity and enables long-term financing for income-generating real estate assets. This policy change is a significant tailwind for the broader REIT market, including industrial REITs, by providing greater access to capital for expansion and development, thereby supporting sector growth and financial stability.

viewpoints.title: Warehousing InvITs poised for growth despite land and construction cost pressures
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings notes that Warehousing InvITs, while currently a smaller segment with Rs 11,500 crore in AUM as of March 31, 2025, are well-positioned for growth. This is driven by buoyant demand from e-commerce, third-party logistics (3PL), and multimodal supply chains. India’s Grade A warehouse stock is projected to exceed 500 million sq ft by CY30 with healthy occupancy levels. However, rising land prices and construction costs relative to rental yields present near-term challenges, leading to a cautious yet positive outlook for the sector.

viewpoints.title: Industrial and warehousing sector demonstrates strong activity driven by key demand segments
viewpoints.description: KPMG in India reports strong activity in the industrial and warehousing sector, with overall leasing reaching 20 million sq. ft. in 1HCY25. This robust performance is primarily attributed to sustained demand from third-party logistics (3PL) providers, the engineering and automobile sectors, and significant support from the e-commerce industry. The consistent demand from these diverse segments underpins a positive outlook for continued growth and development within the warehousing and logistics parks sub-industry.

demand_drivers.description: The rapid growth of online retail necessitates increased warehousing and fulfillment infrastructure to support efficient delivery and inventory management.
Outsourcing of logistics operations by businesses drives demand for modern, efficient warehousing facilities managed by 3PL firms.
Integration of various transport modes requires strategically located logistics parks and warehouses to facilitate seamless movement and storage of goods.

pnl_drivers.description: Projected occupancy levels of around 90% indicate strong demand for available warehouse stock, supporting rental yields and profitability.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected stock of Grade A warehouse space in India.

demand_drivers.description: Growing appetite from large, long-term investors for stable, income-generating real assets, including logistics infrastructure.
InvITs are expanding beyond traditional segments (roads, telecom) into warehousing, offering new investment avenues.

pnl_drivers.description: Stable and high occupancy rates in underlying warehousing assets contribute to consistent rental income for InvITs.
Prudent debt levels in warehousing InvITs support financial stability and investor confidence.

market_sizing.methodology: Asset Under Management (AUM) for warehousing Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) in India.

demand_drivers.description: 3PL companies are primary drivers of leasing activity as they expand their footprint to cater to diverse client needs.
These manufacturing-heavy sectors require significant warehousing space for raw materials, components, and finished goods.
The continuous expansion of online retail fuels demand for modern storage and distribution centers.

market_sizing.methodology: Total leasing volume in the industrial and warehousing sector for the first half of CY25.
